title: vet-flat plan
description: Part of Pea Princess (vet-flat) by Hsien Hao (Jacky) Chen - https://github.com/jacky18008/pea-princess - CC BY 4.0. The planner's output in the role pipeline (references/pipeline.md): what to fetch, what to paste and what to ask, before anybody has read a page. THE PLANNER DECIDES WHAT TO GET, NEVER WHAT SURVIVES. It may add axes, scripts, paste requests and questions to the scaffold that scripts/plan.py prints; it may not drop anything the scaffold marked required, and scripts/plan.py --check says whether it did. There is no verdict in this file, no finding, and no number read off a page: a planner that has read a page has already stopped being a planner.

case.description: A short label for the flat this plan is for. Never an address in a shared file.

budget_mode.description: The budget mode from profile.yaml (references/budget-modes.md). It sets how many axes and how many fetches the plan is allowed to ask for.

tier.description: The fixed-form tier, which decides how many of the fixed questions this run owes an answer to. The mapping lives in the `tiers` block of references/fixed-questions.yaml and nowhere else.

axes.description: The axes this run will work, one entry each, in the order they should be started. Executors are handed one GROUP of these at a time.

fixed_form_ids.description: The fixed-question ids (F1 ... F18) this run owes an answer to, from the tier. Never counted in code: read from references/fixed-questions.yaml.

user_questions.description: Everything to ask the user, ONCE, in one message. Each item says what is wanted, where it comes from and why it matters. An empty list means nothing needs asking.

notes.description: Anything the executors need to know that is not an axis: a postcode that spans two buildings, a listing that names no flat number.

id.description: The axis number, 1 to 12, as in report-schema.json.

name.description: The axis name in plain words, for a human reading the plan.

group.description: The executor group this axis belongs to. One executor takes one group, so axes that share a fetch share a group.

required.description: true when the scaffold put this axis in the plan for this budget mode. A required axis may not be dropped; scripts/plan.py --check fails when one is missing.

scripts.description: The script commands to run for this axis, as argument templates. A placeholder in angle brackets - <postcode>, <lat>, <destination> - is filled in by the executor from the profile or from an earlier item, never guessed.

sources.description: Source ids from references/sources.yaml this axis may read. A source not listed here is not off limits, but adding one is a decision worth writing down.

paste_requests.description: What only the user can supply for this axis, in the words the user will be asked: the page, where it is, and why it matters.

cmd.description: The command line, relative to the skill folder, for example "scripts/epc.py search --postcode <postcode>". One command, no shell pipes, no chaining.

why.description: One short sentence: what this call is for.

required.description: true when the scaffold asked for this call. Defaults to false for a call the planner added.
